name: Cefuroxime
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.indication: Oral: bronchitis exacerbation, uncomplicated skin infection

usual_adult_dose.dose: 750 mg to 1.5 g every 8 hours (life-threatening: 1.5 g every 6 hours; meningitis up to 3 g every 8 hours)
1.5 g before incision, then 750 mg every 8 hours if prolonged

key_interactions.effect: Blocks tubular secretion; higher and longer drug levels (label).

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Antacids, H2 blockers, proton pump inhibitors (oral)
key_interactions.effect: Lower bioavailability of cefuroxime axetil; may cancel the food effect on absorption (label 7.1).
key_interactions.action: Give at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after short-acting antacids; avoid H2 blockers and proton pump inhibitors (label 7.1).

contraindications: Known hypersensitivity (such as anaphylaxis) to cefuroxime or other beta-lactams (penicillins, cephalosporins)

pk.half_life_eskd: Prolonged in severe kidney impairment (label; no value given)
pk.excretion_renal_pct: About 89% of an IV dose unchanged in urine in 8 hours

revision_log.change: Not applied as proposed: the pinned oral label (ANDA065308, 7.1) states 'Administer cefuroxime axetil at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after administration of short-acting antacids. Histamine-2 (H2) antagonists and proton pump inhibitors should be avoided.' Action kept and now attributed to label 7.1; effect adds the food-effect statement.
